6934.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ǵn̥h₁-yé-tor. Compare γίγνομαι (gígnomai), Latin gigno, gnatus and Sanskrit जनति (jánati).

6969.t: From γεννάω (gennắō, “I beget”) + -σις (-sĭs, verbal noun suffix). Compare simple γένεσις (génesis).

6970.t: Compare Old Armenian կամուրջ (kamurǰ, “bridge”) and Hattic 𒄩𒄠𒈬𒊒𒊀 (ḫa-am-mu-ru-waₐ /⁠ḫamuruwa, ḫammuruwa, ḫāmuruwaₐ⁠/, “beam”), with further origin unknown.

6977.t: From earlier διχθά (dĭkhthắ), from δίς (dĭ́s, “twice”). The velar derivation is unclear; compare Sanskrit द्विधा (dvidhā, “by two”), the dh of which might be found in δι-χ-θά.

6917.t: Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *gʷerh₃- (“to devour”). Compare Latin vorāgō.

6918.t: Borrowed from Middle Indic forms like Pali veḷuriya or Prakrit 𑀯𑁂𑀭𑀼𑀮𑀺𑀅 (verulia), from Dravidian, probably named after a city (modern day Bēlūr) in southern India in which the mineral was mined.

6963.t: From γραφή (graphḗ, “drawing, painting, writing, a writing, description, etc.”) + -ικός (-ikós), from γράφω (gráphō).

6945.t: From γένος (génos, “race, stock, kin”) + -ικός (-ĭkós, adjectival suffix).

6976.t: Furnée pointed out that the traditional derivation from *δίκ-σκος (*dík-skos), from δικεῖν (dikeîn, “to cast”) is hardly possible, because the suffix “-σκο-” is rare in nominal derivation.

6982.t: Derived from δέκα (dékă) + -άς (-ắs); compare δυάς (duás), τριάς (triás), τετράς (tetrás), χιλιάς (khiliás), μυριάς (muriás).

6925.t: Probably from Proto-Indo-European *gl̥h₁éys (“weasel, mouse”) and cognate with Latin glīs (“dormouse”), Sanskrit गिरि (girí, “mouse”), though the veracity and existence of the Sanskrit comparandum has been contested.

6940.t: Probably derived from γένεθλον (génethlon) or γενέθλη (genéthlē, “race, stock, family, birthplace”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵenh₁- (“to give birth”) + *-dʰlom (“instrumental suffix”). See also γίγνομαι (gígnomai, “to be born”).

6971.t: Reduplicated formation. It is often connected with grānum (“seed, kernel”) and Old High German kerno (“pit, stone”), which is formally improbable.
